proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no indemnity at all, yet Section 9.3 references "Section 20.5" and the cap carves out indemnification obligations. We have inserted our standard Vendor indemnity (IP, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with the usual notice-and-control procedure, and kept Customer's indemnity narrow.

ops.newText:
Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.

21.5 Indemnification. Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Customer shall give Vendor prompt notice of the claim, and Vendor shall have control of the defence and settlement (provided no settlement imposing liability or admission on Customer is made without Customer's consent), with Customer's reasonable cooperation at Vendor's expense. For an infringement claim, Vendor shall at its expense procure the right to continue use, or modify or replace the affected item so it is non-infringing and materially equivalent, failing which Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive a refund of prepaid Fees. Customer shall indemnify Vendor only against third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of Applicable Law.
